title: Microsoft employees in India can now opt for a buyout: Who qualifies and what it pays
content: Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees, over a quarter of its workforce, in India, the US, the UK and Canada. HR head Amy Coleman announced the Voluntary Exit Offer in a memo to staff. The package matches standard severance, which can run up to 39 weeks of pay. Xbox, Copilot and Windows teams are eligible, sales is excluded, and the deadline is December.

title: Georgia court backs daughter as guardian of mother, 95, amid sibling dispute
content: A dispute between three siblings over their 95-year-old mother's care reached the Georgia Court of Appeals after one son restricted his sister's visits and questions emerged over the handling of their mother's money. The woman, who has advanced dementia, had previously authorised her son to manage her affairs. However, the court upheld her daughter's appointment as guardian.

title: Texas barber, $100 short on rent, returns $128,514 found at ATM

Struggling with rent and financial issues, he made the commendable choice to report this to the authorities. The bags belonged to a Brink’s team who had accidentally left them behind. Though no financial reward was given, the barber's honesty was recognized and celebrated by the police.

title: British historian donates 50 colonial-era Indian paintings to Tate

This diverse collection, meticulously curated by British art historian Charles Greig over 40 years, will be publicly exhibited at Tate Britain in 2028, enhancing public access to these invaluable historical pieces and underscoring the importance of art preservation.

title: Dropbox layoffs: Co-CEO announces 9% job cuts in company memo

title: California brothers face 35 felony charges each over unbuilt backyard homes

title: Delhi HC rejects PIL against passport fee hike for NRIs
content:
File photo: Indian passport

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Wednesday dismissed a PIL challenging the central govt’s decision to increase passport fees for non-resident Indians (NRIs), observing that a 67% hike after a gap of 14 years is not “unreasonable or exorbitant”. Acting chief justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and justice Sanjay Sharma added that the decision to determine the fees falls within the policy domain of the govt and judicial intervention was not warranted. Pravasi Legal Cell filed the petition, alleging discrimination against NRIs, who are required to pay around Rs 11,900 for passports, compared to Rs 2,500 for resident Indians.
